reference: The sampler is James Propp and David Wilson, 'Exact sampling with coupled Markov chains and applications to statistical mechanics', Random Structures and Algorithms 9, 223 to 252 (1996); random tilings are one of their own worked examples. The limit shape measured on the plate is Henry Cohn, Michael Larsen and James Propp, 'The shape of a typical boxed plane partition', New York Journal of Mathematics 4, 137 to 165 (1998). The count of boxed plane partitions is Percy MacMahon, 'Memoir on the theory of the partitions of numbers, Part VI: partitions in two-dimensional space, to which is added an adumbration of the theory of partitions in three-dimensional space', Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A 211, 345 to 373 (1912). The height function that turns a tiling into a stack of cubes is William Thurston, 'Conway's tiling groups', American Mathematical Monthly 97, 757 to 773 (1990). How long this chain needs is David Wilson, 'Mixing times of lozenge tiling and card shuffling Markov chains', Annals of Applied Probability 14, 274 to 325 (2004).
equation: h(x, y) ∈ [0, c] weakly decreasing;  heat bath h(x, y) ~ U{max(h(x+1,y), h(x,y+1)) … min(h(x−1,y), h(x,y−1))};  run −T → 0 from ⊥ and ⊤ on one fixed set of maps, doubling T until they agree, and read the common value at 0
limitations: The arctic radius and free area the plate prints against the limit shape come from a local ring-3 frozen test and disagree with the Cohn-Larsen-Propp ellipse beyond their error bars at every size tested: over independent seeds the radius reads 1.0060 ± 0.0004 at 24,24,24, 1.0016 ± 0.0005 at 32,32,32 and 0.9979 ± 0.0006 at 48,48,48 (free area 0.9185, 0.9104 and 0.9035 against 0.9069), crossing the limit rather than converging to it. This is one of the two reasons the status is partial; see validation/LOZENGE.md.

The per-plate free-area error bar undercovers: the scatter across seeds is 1.13, 1.27 and 1.18 times the root-mean-square bar at 32,32,32, 48,48,48 and 24,40,46 (95 per cent intervals exclude or touch 1). The radius bar is calibrated or conservative. This is the second reason for the partial status.
Exhaustive uniformity covers the boxes 2,2,2, 2,2,3, 2,3,4 and 3,3,3 plus the volume law on 4,4,4; larger hexagons use the same code but are not enumerated here.
Uniformity probabilities assume the seeded draws behave as independent uniform variates; fixed PRNG samples do not prove it.
Print evidence covers seven recipes on one renderer (headless Chromium 141, SwiftShader, Linux). Grain is omitted from the vector sheet by design.
remaining: Either scope the arctic readout out of the validated claim as a finite-size diagnostic or measure a boundary that converges (for example corner-connected frozen regions with a finite-size extrapolation), and make the free-area bar cover or say where it does not; then rerun node tools/lozenge-science.js --write and review promotion.
Extend print evidence to other renderers and more recipes.

numerical.scope: The tab's own makeJob, runJob, buildTiling, corners, classify, measureArctic, ellipseOf, macmahonLog10 and samplerSelfTest run unmodified in Node: exhaustive enumeration of tilings and plane partitions up to 4,4,4 and the drawn-tiling bijection; sampled frequencies on four boxes and the 4,4,4 volume law; the arctic radius, free area and self-test over 470 independent full-regenerate plates on 24,24,24, 32,32,32, 48,48,48 and 24,40,46; seven complete rendered recipes with every SVG rhombus and curve point, every PNG byte and the shell vector RIP.
numerical.criteria: Direct tiling count = plane partition count = MacMahon product (BigInt) on five boxes; drawn tilings distinct and in the enumeration; ellipseOf equal to the tangency solution within 1e-12; per box, Pearson chi-square p >= 0.001, no tiling undrawn, tiling and rhombus-placement probabilities inside a simultaneous Hoeffding bound and a Bonferroni z bound at alpha 0.001; volume chi-square p >= 0.001 and mean within 3.29 sigma of 32; every plate exact and sound; self-test deviations mean within 3 standard errors of 0 and pooled p >= 0.001; SVG coordinates <= 0.00501 px, PNG bytes <= 1, shell print equal to the rasterized reference SVG, state unchanged. The limit-shape readings and their bar calibration are reported, not pass criteria.
numerical.benchmark: Direct enumeration of lozenge tilings of the hexagon's unit triangles and separate enumeration of plane partitions against MacMahon's product (1912); exact rhombus placement probabilities and the exact 4,4,4 volume distribution from those enumerations; the Cohn-Larsen-Propp inscribed ellipse solved independently from its tangency; the Propp-Wilson exactness claim tested against all of these; geometry rebuilt from the cube stack.
numerical.failureControl: A biased monotone update (u^2), reading the state at the meeting time, and a coalescence check over half the sites each fail uniformity on 2,2,2 and 3,3,3 (chi-square 63 to 2,044,985) and are flagged by the tab's own self-test (z 4.7 to 65); another seed's tiling fails the SVG check; a one-pixel shift fails the PNG check.
numerical.limitations: The arctic readout disagrees with the limit shape beyond its error bars at every size and its free-area bar undercovers at 32 and 48; exhaustive uniformity only up to 3,3,3 plus the 4,4,4 volume law; one renderer.

print.scope: Seven recipes loaded through the recipe hash in a temporary copy of dist/studio.html (11,11,11 with strokes; 24,40,46 with both curves; 48,48,8 frozen with the predicted ellipse; 32,32,32; 20,20,40 flat with strokes; 36,36,36 frozen at 1:1 with both curves; 16,16,16 height color with the hairline seam; grain 0), exported at 8 in and 300 ppi by the module and by the shell's own Export.
print.criteria: Browser heights, CFTP times, sector radii and bars equal the Node regenerate() run; orientations and frozen flags equal the independent reconstruction; every SVG rhombus and curve point within 0.00501 px of geometry rebuilt from the cube stack with the documented colors, strokes and dashes; module PNG within one level of an independent painting; shell PNG identical to the rasterized reference SVG; shell SVG carries the same geometry and provenance; state unchanged after export.
print.benchmark: Direct enumeration of lozenge tilings of the hexagon's unit triangles and separate enumeration of plane partitions against MacMahon's product (1912); exact rhombus placement probabilities and the exact 4,4,4 volume distribution from those enumerations; the Cohn-Larsen-Propp inscribed ellipse solved independently from its tangency; the Propp-Wilson exactness claim tested against all of these; geometry rebuilt from the cube stack.
print.failureControl: Another seed's tiling of the same hexagon fails the SVG check; the reference painting shifted by one pixel differs in 295,226 to 1,276,675 channels.
print.limitations: Seven recipes, one renderer; grain is not in the vector sheet.

domain.parameters: Boxes 2,2,2, 2,2,3, 2,3,4, 3,3,3 and 4,4,4 (exhaustive; the smallest are below the UI minimum of 3 and run through the same makeJob and runJob); hexagons 24,24,24, 32,32,32, 48,48,48 and 24,40,46 at ring 3 with the exact sampler; the seven print recipes in validation/results/lozenge-science.json.
domain.conditions: Coupling from the past from the empty and full boxes with the module counter hash keyed as build() keys it (recipe seeds lozenge-uniform-<box>-<i>, lozenge-volume-4x4x4-<i>, lozenge-arctic-<box>-<i>, lozenge-print-<k>); every plate exact, none fell back to the heat bath; no grain in the print fixtures; exports must preserve recipe and state.
domain.resolution: Exact integer tilings and heights; sampling errors as stated (standard errors over 60 to 200 independent seeds per hexagon; chi-square intervals for calibration ratios); prints from 1,386 by 2,400 to 2,400 by 2,400 px at 8 in and 300 ppi.
domain.precision: Integer heights and Binary64 statistics; SVG coordinates rounded to 0.01 px; RGBA8 raster; Node 22 and headless Chromium 141 with SwiftShader recorded in the results.
